plan.title: GO BP over-representation in AD lesional vs control skin
plan.analytical_narrative: The de_results.csv table already carries a DESeq2 treated(AD lesional)-vs-control contrast for 12000 genes across 6 vs 6 unpaired skin samples. The research question asks specifically which GO biological processes are over-represented among the significant genes — this is an over-representation analysis (ORA) on a discrete gene list, not a ranked test, so the primary method is clusterProfiler::enrichGO with the tested genes as the background universe. Because ORA on a short significant list is underpowered and threshold-sensitive (a documented risk when <~50 genes pass), we first check the list size and flag if the finding is too small to trust; a preranked fgsea GSEA against MSigDB GO:BP on the DESeq2 Wald statistic runs in parallel as an explicit secondary/robustness check per the standing guidance that ORA and ranked methods can disagree and neither is 'the truth'. We reduce the many nested, redundant significant GO terms with rrvgo semantic-similarity clustering so the deliverable is a handful of representative processes rather than hundreds of overlapping nested terms. The library-size caveat on sample_01 is noted but the input here is a delivered results table, not raw counts, so that check is inherited from the upstream DE run and is reported as such, not re-run. A companion sample-structure QC on the counts file is included for completeness/transparency of the report since counts.csv and metadata.csv are also provided.

input.query: HGNC gene symbol annotation human ensembl to symbol

steps.method: DESeq2 vst(blind) + PCA + sample distance heatmap
clusterProfiler enrichGO (GO Biological Process) with rrvgo term reduction
fgsea preranked GSEA on DESeq2 Wald statistic against GO BP (secondary check)
